summary: AI observability tools provide visibility into how LLM applications behave in production, tracking traces, latency, token usage, costs, and output quality to help teams debug issues and control spend. As LLM API costs can scale rapidly and model behavior is non-deterministic, observability is essential for maintaining reliability, evaluating performance, and preventing runaway expenses. In 2026, these platforms have become a core part of any serious AI engineering stack.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, LLM calls, agent chains, evaluations, latency, and token-based cost across LLM applications (tightly integrated with LangChain).
features: Detailed trace and span visualization for chains and agents
Dataset creation and automated LLM evaluations
tools.pricing: Free tier limited to ~5,000 monthly traces; Plus plan with per-seat pricing plus usage-based trace charges. Trace costs often run roughly 5-10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that need deep tracing, evaluation, and debugging in one integrated platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM requests and responses via a proxy/gateway, metering request volume, token usage, latency, and computed cost across providers.
features: Drop-in proxy gateway for request logging
Cost tracking and per-request cost computation
Caching to reduce redundant API calls
Prompt and session analytics with alerts
tools.pricing: Free up to 10,000 requests/month; paid usage at approximately $79 per 100,000 traces/requests with team plans available.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a lightweight, provider-agnostic gateway focused on cost control, caching, and quick-to-adopt logging.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML experiments, model training runs, LLM traces and evaluations (via W&B Weave), metrics, artifacts, and production model performance.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/individual use; team and enterprise plans priced per seat with usage-based components. Custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that need unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability across the full model lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, embeddings, drift, data quality, evaluations, and traces (including open-source Arize Phoenix).
features: LLM and ML observability with drift and quality monitoring
Open-source Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source; Arize AX cloud platform offers a free tier with paid pro and custom enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Enterprises running ML and LLM models in production that need robust monitoring, drift detection, and RAG/embedding analysis.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, costs, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores across LLM and agent applications.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
Self-hostable with SDKs and framework integrations
tools.pricing: Open source and free to self-host; managed cloud offers a free hobby tier with usage-based Pro and Team plans.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a flexible, open-source-first observability platform with the option to self-host for data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, and metrics using OpenTelemetry standards, exportable to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Integration with existing observability backends (Datadog, Grafana, etc.)
tools.pricing: Free and open source; optional Traceloop managed platform with free tier and paid plans for hosted analytics.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation integrated into their existing observability stack.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., via a gateway like Helicone) so identical prompts don't trigger redundant paid API calls.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model, using smaller or distilled models for simple queries and reserving frontier models for complex reasoning.
Reduce token usage by trimming prompts, compressing context, limiting retrieved RAG chunks, and setting sensible max-token limits on outputs.
Set budgets, rate limits, and alerts on token/cost dashboards to catch runaway spend early, and batch requests where latency allows to improve efficiency.
